about: packages/mutation/src/props.json: the mutation story's part of the catalogue of 3D sets (props; docs/props.md, tools/packages/SPEC.md "Miniatures"): what the design room's card of each of its miniatures shows; code is authoritative

sets.shows: A text in four letters copied with swaps: a 24-pair DNA helix, eight letters peeling into tiles (ACGTTAGC), two copies with swaps flashing, then one letter opened into its two qubits, a mix of letters and read-outs spinning like a coin and piling into four heaps as tall as the chances.
sets.frame: Centred on the origin; helix vertical; tiles in a row.
sets.size: not stated in the manifest (see views)

params.name: letters_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: letters_helix
params.meaning: the helix (both strands, rungs, backbones); it turns by t

params.name: letters_peel
params.meaning: the ancestor's eight letters grow out of their rungs as tiles, peel away one after another (a zipper) and line up as a row with its strand behind

params.name: letters_copy1
params.meaning: copy 1 slides out of the ancestor's row (down, left and forward), a dashed green trace behind it

params.name: letters_mut1
params.meaning: copy 1's two swaps: the first over 0-0.5, the second over 0.5-1 (flip, flash, ring, white frame)

params.name: letters_copy2
params.meaning: copy 2 slides out (further down, right and forward)

params.name: letters_mut2
params.meaning: copy 2's two swaps, as copy 1's

params.name: letters_open
params.meaning: the ancestor's first tile (A) comes forward and grows (0-0.45), the rows fade (0.05-0.5), the two qubits open out of it (0.35-1)

params.name: letters_code
params.meaning: which two-qubit code is shown, 0..3 (00, 01, 10, 11): the tile turns over and each arrow flips on its own

params.name: letters_mix
params.meaning: 0 the pure code, 1 the mix: the arrows tilt (amplitudes blended), the tile turns into ? with its ring of four shares

params.name: letters_target
params.meaning: the mix: 0 the rule's mix after letters_time from the code's letter (the story's model, uneven), 1 the even mix (a quarter each)

params.name: letters_time
params.meaning: the branch length for the rule's mix (swaps per letter, 0..3)

params.name: letters_reads
params.meaning: how many read-outs

params.name: letters_seed
params.meaning: which read-outs come out (MMATH.sample(p, seed, k))

data.text: Figure 1's sequences and swaps typed in from the poster; mixes and read-outs computed live by MMATH (example numbers).

sets.notes: Cheap (6 ms). British spelling. letters_code, letters_target, letters_seed are steps. Exports api (READ_MAX, mix, counts, reads, chances, bloch).

sets.shows: A family tree in 3D (8 tips, 14 branches) that grows up from its root as a level of change rises (a branch rises by its length), every swap simulated, letters riding up each branch; a gear (machine) on every branch; and the poster's species tree. You walk round it and look up into it.
sets.frame: Root at (0, -1, 0); tips on a ring round the vertical; the species tree in the same frame (stem set draws in it).
sets.size: tree ~2.06 units tall with letters, widest radius 1.18

params.name: tree_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: tree_species
params.meaning: 0 the family tree, 1 the species tree; in between a crossfade (a plain param: the engine eases it)

params.name: tree_grow
params.meaning: the level of change rising from the root past the highest tip (0 nothing, 1 all grown); a thin green ring marks it while it rises

params.name: tree_seq
params.meaning: the letters: the ancestor's arc at the root, the rows riding up, the tips' rows

params.name: tree_hi
params.meaning: lights the long and the short branch (tree.highlight: for seed 1, branch 10, 0.47 swaps per letter, 4 swaps, and branch 7, 0.15, 1 swap) in green, dims the rest, and

params.name: tree_gears
params.meaning: a gear on every branch (at a third of its way up, the branch its axle), winding up to its turn (2.4 x turnAngle(len)); coupling gears (the double band) on the species

params.name: tree_flow
params.meaning: the machines run: packets rise through the grown branches (a bead every 1.1 of height, rising 0.55 a second, by t), the gears turn on (faster on longer branches), and

params.name: tree_q
params.meaning: the glass "?" at the species tree's root (the unknown ancestor; it pulses)

params.name: tree_seed
params.meaning: which family tree (any integer from 1). Step param

params.name: tree_speed
params.meaning: how fast letters change: index into [0.5, 1, 2, 4] (a factor on every branch length; it changes the mutations, not the drawing)

params.name: tree_pick
params.meaning: a picked branch (0..13, -1 none): lit cyan with its rise measured, its gear lit; the others dim

sets.notes: In a headset it eases into the stand view (about 1.6 m tall, nothing within 0.35 m of the eyes); the up view is screens only. tree_seed, tree_speed, tree_pick are steps. 11 views. Exports api (speeds, model, tree, species, highlight, branch, pick, mid, tips).

sets.shows: The rule of change: four letter balls at the corners of a pyramid joined by rate arrows, the pyramid of mixes and a point gliding along its path, the compiler (a drum with a gear), the machine for one branch (copy the parent's letter, then turn it), its circuit and the turn blocks opening into their simple steps.
sets.frame: Centred on the origin; A at the top, C front left, G back, T front right.
sets.size: pyramid x +-0.93, y -0.5 to 1.2; machine x -1.15 to 1.05

params.name: rule_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: rule_balls
params.meaning: the balls grow (0-0.5) and the arrows draw from tail to head (0.2-1)

params.name: rule_flow
params.meaning: light running along the arrows

params.name: rule_pyr
params.meaning: the pyramid forms: edges from the corners (0-0.6), faces (0.3-1), corner tiles (0.5-1); the balls shrink into the corners (0.1-0.8), the arrows fade (0-0.5)

params.name: rule_path
params.meaning: the mix point, its trail and the path ahead, points 1-3, the long-run ring, the threads

params.name: rule_time
params.meaning: the branch length / time (swaps per letter, 0..3): where the point is on the path; in the machine the dial, the gears, the child's arrows and mix, the circuit's angles

params.name: rule_model
params.meaning: 0 even (JC69), 1 transitions (K80, κ 4), 2 uneven (the story's GTR example)

params.name: rule_start
params.meaning: the path's start letter (A C G T). Step param

params.name: rule_compile
params.meaning: the drum appears (0-0.3); the pyramid shrinks above it (0-0.4) and drops in (0.4-0.8); its gear spins up

params.name: rule_machine
params.meaning: the machine comes out of the drum part by part (staggered, 0-0.8), the drum shrinks and goes (0.45-0.9)

params.name: rule_parent
params.meaning: the parent's letter. Step param (its tile turns over, its arrows flip)

params.name: rule_copy
params.meaning: the copy: the head moves over the parent (0-0.12), lifts its letter (0.12-0.28), carries it (0.28-0.5), stamps it on the child (0.5-0.66), returns (0.66-0.85); the

params.name: rule_circuit
params.meaning: the circuit under the machine: wires grow left to right (0-0.6), inputs, copy gates, turn blocks

params.name: rule_simple
params.meaning: the turn blocks open into their simple steps

params.name: rule_run
params.meaning: pulses run along the wires (by t)

labels.text: Bigger ball · more common in the long run
Compiler · a rule in, a circuit out
Copy · the parent’s letter onto the child
Turn · as far as the branch is long
The child’s mix · the same path
Simple steps · 12 turns of one qubit, 12 links

data.text: Three example substitution models (JC69, K80 and the story's GTR example) computed live; the circuit's angles and simple steps checked by a state-vector run.

sets.notes: rule_model, rule_start, rule_parent are steps. Exports api (models, mix, longRun, rates, angles, turn, steps, shown).

sets.shows: Letters that work together: an RNA strand folds into a stem of six pairs, one letter changes alone and its rung snaps, a coupling makes the pair change together, the count of combinations (16, 64, about a million) against qubits, then three fields of 2,000 rebuilt ancestors on the species tree.
sets.frame: In the tree set's frame; chapter 6 at the origin with the tree hidden, chapter 7 at the species tree.
sets.size: stem ~radius 1; fields in front of the root

params.name: stem_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: stem_strand
params.meaning: the close-up's strand: its 16 tiles pop in left to right with the backbone

params.name: stem_fold
params.meaning: 0 a straight row, to 0.55 a hairpin folding round its loop, to 1 the twisted stem (pair 5 square to the story's view); rungs from 0.75

params.name: stem_break
params.meaning: pair 5's top letter flips C -> A at 0.5 (a flash, framed white), its rung pulls back into two stubs (0.5-0.75), a red cross (0.55-0.85), the stem bulges there; back to

params.name: stem_couple
params.meaning: the coupling gear over pair 5 (the double band along the rung), winding in

params.name: stem_both
params.meaning: pair 5 changes both letters at once at 0.5 (C -> T, G -> A, framed white, a flash), the gear turns half round, the rung lights cyan: it holds

params.name: stem_count
params.meaning: 0..3: to 1 the 4 x 4 square of tile pairs beside the stem (the six matching pairs lit, the rest dim)

params.name: stem_qubits
params.meaning: a row of 20 qubits under it all (two per letter, each pair holding a letter's mix: MMATH.path at the story's points, MMATH.bloch), appearing left to right

params.name: stem_species
params.meaning: the three species' stems on the species tree's tips, small, upright, facing the viewer, broken pairs as red crosses; letters that differ from the true ancestor framed

params.name: stem_fields
params.meaning: three fields of 2,000 tiny stems sprout in front of the root (left to right: letter by letter, exact pair model, coupled circuit), each at its own moment: lit in the

params.name: stem_named
params.meaning: how many fields' tags show, left to right (0.5: the first tag half in): they come as the narrator names each field

params.name: stem_sort
params.meaning: the stems whose six pairs all hold walk to the front rows of their field (in their random order): a lit block whose depth is the share

params.name: stem_truth
params.meaning: the true ancestor's stem, big at the root (in front of the species tree's "?", which the story fades with tree_q), its one broken pair

params.name: stem_examples
params.meaning: one rebuilt ancestor per method stands before its field (Figure 5's in the story; the most likely one, best, live), letters that differ from the truth framed white; the

params.name: stem_src
params.meaning: 0 the authors' test (their shares, Figure 5's examples), 1 this example computed live (MMATH.rebuild with stem_w and stem_seed)

params.name: stem_w
params.meaning: the pair favour w, 1 to 30 (live only: the authors' test is w = 8)

params.name: stem_seed
params.meaning: the rebuild's seed (which 2,000 ancestors; also the crowd's shuffle)

params.name: stem_method
params.meaning: a method lit, the other fields dimmed: index into MMATH.METHODS (0 indep, 1 coupled, 2 exact), -1 all

Pair broken · C became A alone
C–G became T–A · the pair holds
20 qubits · two per letter, for all ten

data.text: The poster's Figure 5 stems and shares (10 %, 43 %, 20 %, quarter with all pairs matched) typed in, shown only "in the authors' test"; the live example uses our stand-in coupling (MMATH.Pcoupled), labelled so. Never say the coupled circuit is "better".
